scope: Two synthetic controlled replays only; no new learner deliveries or persisted feedback jobs. Prior six observed outcomes unchanged.
history_use: Four observations reach the experienced case request and none reach the sparse case. The experienced raw response is withheld and its resulting deterministic history sentence is generic; useful history-conditioned Qwen guidance is not demonstrated. Different graph and prior-context selection from the historical run prevent attributing changed behavior solely to history.
non_revealing: The sparse raw output was accepted by automated checks yet directly prescribes a replacement join type, contrary to the explicit non-revealing instruction. It is not a complete SQL solution but reveals a concrete key repair; independent non-revealing assessment fails. The experienced raw output also prescribes a replacement join and suggests the correct identifier count may be wrong; the quality guard withheld it. The fallback names a join as a review topic but does not prescribe a replacement join.

cases.finding: Raw feedback wrongly questions the correct COUNT(identifier) component and prescribes a replacement join; the guard prevents its delivery. Deterministic replay fallback offers generic history language, not a demonstrated useful model personalization.
Automated validation accepted the raw response despite explicit instruction violation: it prescribes the replacement join type. This is a controlled replay outcome, not a new learner-delivered job.

limits: Two examples establish neither broad model quality nor exhaustive safety properties; no prompt was changed and no additional inference was run.
